value.body: A cardiac care technologist runs tests that show how the heart is working and assists cardiologists during procedures. Employers include hospitals with cardiology departments, heart centres and diagnostic chains. A typical day involves recording ECGs and stress tests, preparing patients, and in larger hospitals, working in the cath lab during angiograms and angioplasties.

items.label: Common tests
items.value: ECG, Holter, TMT (stress test), echo support

items.label: Regulation
items.value: Allied health professions fall under the NCAHP Act, 2021

items.label: Angioplasties (PCI) in a year
items.note: Reported by ~709 cath-lab centres, about 70% of the country's cath labs
items.source: CSI National Interventional Council data, Indian Heart Journal 2020

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Graduates usually join hospitals as technologists after their internship; cath lab roles typically come after some time in non-invasive testing. Emergency and on-call duty is common in hospitals that do emergency heart procedures.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Sterile technique in the cath lab

value.title: At a glance
items: Cath lab work involves radiation safety precautions and on-call hours.
Next roles: senior or chief technologist, echo specialist, cath lab in-charge.

value.title: Angioplasties (PCI) reported per year
value.note: Voluntary reporting; centres reporting rose from ~404 (2013) to ~709 (2018), so part of the rise reflects wider coverage. Rounded.
value.source: CSI National Interventional Council data, Indian Heart Journal 2020
